V: Migraine with aura or migraine variant: Family history of migraines, unilateral throbbing headache, no systemic symptoms
Intracranial hemorrhage or vascular event (e.g., subdural hematoma, stroke): Unilateral, severe headache; however, sudden onset and neurological signs absent
I: Meningitis or encephalitis: Would expect fever, neck stiffness, systemic symptoms which are absent
Sinusitis: Unlikely without sinus symptoms or fever
N: Brain tumor: New headache but typically progressive, associated neurological deficits absent
D: Tension-type headache: Usually bilateral and less severe, but can present atypically
Nutritional deficiency headache: No indication of deficiency or dietary changes
I2: Medication side effect or withdrawal headache: No medication changes or substance use reported
C: Congenital vascular malformation (e.g., AVM): Could present with headache but typically earlier or with hemorrhage
A: Allergic or immune-mediated headache: No rash or systemic symptoms
T: Trauma-induced headache (e.g., concussion): No history of trauma
E: Hypertension-induced headache: Patient has no personal history, though family history present
Metabolic derangement (e.g., hypoglycemia): No symptoms or history supporting
